# TetherCam

> Your iPhone, instead of a webcam. Two free apps and one USB cable connect an
> iPhone camera to Mac apps such as Zoom, Teams, Google Meet and FaceTime.
> No Wi-Fi, cloud, account or shared Apple Account. The OBS plugin is a separate
> receiver for streaming and recording with video and microphone audio.

Verified release facts, 2026-09-10:
- iPhone App Store app: 0.2.0, free, iOS 17 or later.
- Mac app: 0.3.0, free, macOS 14 or later, Apple silicon and Intel.
- OBS plugin: 0.3.0, free, macOS 12 or later and OBS Studio 30 or later.
The three components have separate distribution states. A GitHub release does not
mean the same iPhone version has passed App Review.

## Use the iPhone as a webcam in Zoom, Teams, Meet or FaceTime

Install TetherCam on the iPhone and TetherCam for Mac. Connect a USB data cable and
tap Trust on the iPhone the first time. Drag the Mac app into Applications with
Finder, open it, and allow its camera extension once in System Settings > General >
Login Items & Extensions > Camera Extensions. This approval needs an administrator
password. Select the camera TetherCam in your call app.

The Mac app lives in the menu bar and outputs 1920x1080 video at 30 fps. It carries
video only; select a separate microphone in the call. Keep the iPhone unlocked with
TetherCam in the foreground. A portrait phone is pillarboxed into the output frame.
The phone accepts one receiver: run either the Mac app or the OBS plugin, not both.

Verified with an iPhone 15 Pro Max in QuickTime Player, Photo Booth, FaceTime, Google
Meet in Chrome, Safari, Chrome and ffmpeg on 2026-09-09, plus Zoom 7.1.5 and Microsoft
Teams on 2026-09-10. Other apps using the system camera list have not been individually
tested here. Restart a call app if its camera list is stale after installation.

- Mac download: https://github.com/Kanevry/tethercam/releases/latest/download/TetherCam-mac.dmg
- iPhone download: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tethercam/id6808997521
- Homebrew alternative: `brew tap kanevry/tethercam`, then `brew install --cask tethercam`
- Setup and troubleshooting: https://tethercam.app/install#mac-app

The Mac download is Developer ID signed and notarized. It is not a Mac App Store app.

## Use the iPhone as a camera and microphone in OBS

Install the OBS plugin on the Mac and TetherCam on the iPhone, then connect a USB
data cable. Restart OBS after installing. Choose Tools > TetherCam: Add iPhone camera
to current scene. Keep the phone unlocked and its app open. Do not run the Mac receiver
app at the same time.

With iPhone app 0.2.0 or later and a compatible plugin, microphone audio reaches the
OBS mixer for recordings and streams. The app has a mute switch. OBS can pass the
picture to another app through Start Virtual Camera, but that virtual camera carries
video only. A call still needs a separately selected microphone.

- OBS installer: https://github.com/Kanevry/tethercam/releases/latest/download/TetherCam-obs-plugin.pkg
- OBS setup: https://tethercam.app/install#mac-plugin
- Homebrew: `brew tap kanevry/tethercam`, then `brew install --cask tethercam-obs`

## How this differs from Continuity Camera

Continuity Camera also supports USB. TetherCam uses a separate transport through
usbmuxd and does not depend on the Continuity handshake, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a shared
Apple Account. Bernhard built it after Continuity connected but showed a black picture
on his own setup. TetherCam is for iPhone and Mac; no Windows, Linux or Android receiver
ships today. It is free and open source, with no paid tier, account or tracking.

## Image quality and measurements

The iPhone encodes HEVC in hardware. The app provides lens selection, automatic
horizon leveling, diagnostics and double-tap camera switching. The Mac app outputs
1080p30; the OBS path supports 1080p30 and 1080p60.

On one setup (iPhone 15 Pro Max, M4 Pro Mac, OBS 32.2.2), USB ping round trip was about
1 ms, first frame after connection about 90 ms, and reconnect after cable pull about
1.3 seconds. These are transport and startup measurements, not end-to-end camera
latency. End-to-end camera latency has not been measured here.

The 54-second OBS demonstration is a recording of an earlier build:
https://tethercam.app/#demo. Generated studio scenes in the marketing images are
illustrations, not recordings that prove image quality or connection speed.
